title: Voz pasiva en informes
explanation: Se usa para describir procesos o resultados sin decir quién lo hizo — muy común en informes técnicos y actualizaciones de proyecto.
examples: The samples were tested last week.
Three formulations have been developed so far.
The report will be sent by Friday.
exercisePrompt: Transforma a voz pasiva: "Alguien probó las muestras ayer."
exerciseAnswer: The samples were tested yesterday.

title: Estilo indirecto (reported speech)
explanation: Sirve para trasladar en una reunión lo que dijo un cliente o compañero, sin citarlo literalmente.
examples: She said the order would arrive on Monday.
He told us the price had increased.
They mentioned they were considering other suppliers.
exercisePrompt: Pasa a estilo indirecto: El cliente dijo: "We need the samples by Friday."
exerciseAnswer: The client said they needed the samples by Friday.

title: Primer condicional
explanation: Para condiciones reales o probables en el futuro — muy útil al negociar plazos o condiciones.
examples: If the batch fails the test, we'll need to rework the formula.
We'll ship the order if the payment clears today.
If you send the data sheet, I'll review it this afternoon.
exercisePrompt: Completa: "If the client ___ (agree) to the new price, we ___ (start) production next week."
exerciseAnswer: agrees, we will start

title: Segundo condicional
explanation: Para situaciones hipotéticas o improbables en el presente/futuro — útil para plantear escenarios en una reunión.
examples: If we had a bigger budget, we would test more formulations.
I would call the supplier if I were you.
If the price dropped, we would order more.
exercisePrompt: Traduce: "Si tuviéramos más tiempo, probaríamos otra fórmula."
exerciseAnswer: If we had more time, we would test another formula.

title: Tercer condicional
explanation: Para hipótesis sobre el pasado (lo que habría pasado si...) — muy común al analizar errores o incidencias ya cerradas.
examples: If we had tested it earlier, we would have caught the issue.
She wouldn't have called if it hadn't been urgent.
If the shipment had left on time, it would have arrived by now.
exercisePrompt: Traduce: "Si hubiéramos revisado la ficha técnica, habríamos visto el error."
exerciseAnswer: If we had checked the data sheet, we would have seen the error.

title: Oraciones de relativo
explanation: Para añadir información sobre algo o alguien sin abrir una frase nueva — hace tu inglés menos entrecortado.
examples: The client who called yesterday wants a bigger discount.
This is the formula that failed the stability test.
The supplier whose prices increased is based in Germany.
exercisePrompt: Combina en una frase: "The batch failed. The batch was tested last week."
exerciseAnswer: The batch that was tested last week failed.

title: Deducción presente (must/might/can't)
explanation: Para expresar lo probable en el presente sin afirmar con certeza — clave para sonar natural especulando en una reunión.
examples: The line isn't ready, they must still be testing it.
She might be in another meeting.
That can't be right — the numbers don't add up.
exercisePrompt: Traduce: "Seguramente todavía están probando el lote."
exerciseAnswer: They must still be testing the batch.

title: Deducción pasada (must/might/can't + have)
explanation: La misma idea de deducción, pero sobre algo que ya pasó — muy usada al analizar qué pudo haber fallado.
examples: The batch must have failed during transport.
They might have missed the email.
He can't have seen the report yet.
exercisePrompt: Traduce: "No pueden haber probado todas las muestras tan rápido."
exerciseAnswer: They can't have tested all the samples that fast.

title: used to / would (hábitos pasados)
explanation: Para hablar de cómo se hacían las cosas antes, en contraste con ahora — útil al explicar procesos que han cambiado.
examples: We used to test everything manually before we got the new equipment.
He would always double-check the formula before sending it.
They didn't use to require a CoA for this ingredient.
exercisePrompt: Traduce: "Antes solíamos usar otro proveedor."
exerciseAnswer: We used to use a different supplier.

title: Comparativos avanzados (the more..., by far)
explanation: Para reforzar comparaciones de forma más natural que "very" o "more" sueltos.
examples: The more we test, the more confident we are in the formula.
This is by far the most stable version we've developed.
The sooner we confirm, the better.
exercisePrompt: Traduce: "Cuanto antes confirmemos el pedido, antes podremos enviarlo."
exerciseAnswer: The sooner we confirm the order, the sooner we can ship it.

title: Inversión enfática
explanation: Anteponer palabras como "Not only", "Never" o "Rarely" invierte el orden sujeto-verbo y da un tono más formal y enfático — muy C1.
examples: Not only did the batch fail, but the report was also late.
Never have we faced such a delay.
Rarely does a client change the spec this late.
exercisePrompt: Traduce con inversión: "No solo se retrasó el envío, sino que también llegó dañado."
exerciseAnswer: Not only was the shipment delayed, but it also arrived damaged.

title: Cleft sentences (It was... / What...)
explanation: Sirven para poner el foco en una parte concreta de la frase — muy útil para dejar clara la causa de un problema.
examples: It was the supplier who caused the delay.
What we need is a faster approval process.
It's the packaging that's causing the issue.
exercisePrompt: Traduce: "Lo que necesitamos es más tiempo para las pruebas."
exerciseAnswer: What we need is more time for testing.

title: Condicionales mixtos
explanation: Mezclan una condición pasada con una consecuencia presente (o viceversa) — muy natural al hablar de errores con efectos actuales.
examples: If we had tested it properly, we wouldn't be dealing with this now.
If she were more experienced, she would have caught the error.
If the formula were more stable, we wouldn't have had to recall it.
exercisePrompt: Traduce: "Si hubiéramos elegido otro proveedor, no tendríamos este problema ahora."
exerciseAnswer: If we had chosen a different supplier, we wouldn't have this problem now.

title: Oraciones de participio (Having.../Given that...)
explanation: Permiten condensar dos frases en una de forma elegante — suena mucho más fluido que encadenar "and" o "because".
examples: Having finished the stability tests, we can move to scale-up.
Given that the results are positive, we'll proceed with production.
Having reviewed the data, I think we're ready to launch.
exercisePrompt: Traduce: "Habiendo completado las pruebas, podemos pasar a la siguiente fase."
exerciseAnswer: Having completed the tests, we can move to the next phase.

title: Matización (hedging)
explanation: Frases para suavizar una opinión sin sonar tajante — imprescindible en negociación y feedback delicado.
examples: It could be argued that the price is too high for this market.
I'd tend to say the formula needs more work.
Arguably, this is our strongest product yet.
exercisePrompt: Traduce con matización: "Podría decirse que el precio es demasiado alto."
exerciseAnswer: It could be argued that the price is too high.

title: do/does/did enfático
explanation: Añadir "do/does/did" delante del verbo da énfasis a algo que se pone en duda — muy útil para defender algo con firmeza sin subir el tono.
examples: We do understand your concerns about the delay.
The formula did pass the stability test, despite the delay.
I did send the report yesterday.
exercisePrompt: Traduce con énfasis: "Sí que enviamos la muestra la semana pasada."
exerciseAnswer: We did send the sample last week.

title: Futuro perfecto y continuo
explanation: Para proyectar en qué punto estará algo en una fecha futura concreta — muy usado en reuniones de seguimiento de proyecto.
examples: By next month, we will have finished the stability testing.
This time next week, we'll be presenting the results to the client.
By the time you arrive, we'll have already started the meeting.
exercisePrompt: Traduce: "Para el viernes, habremos terminado el informe."
exerciseAnswer: By Friday, we will have finished the report.

title: wish / if only
explanation: Para expresar deseo o arrepentimiento sobre el presente o el pasado — útil para reconocer un fallo con matiz humano, no solo técnico.
examples: I wish we had tested this formula earlier.
If only the supplier had warned us about the delay.
I wish the price were lower.
exercisePrompt: Traduce: "Ojalá hubiéramos revisado esto antes."
exerciseAnswer: I wish we had reviewed this earlier.

title: Causativo (have/get something done)
explanation: Para expresar que otra persona o empresa hace algo por encargo tuyo — frecuente al hablar de laboratorios externos o subcontratas.
examples: We had the samples tested by an external lab.
They got the packaging redesigned last quarter.
We need to have this formula approved before launch.
exercisePrompt: Traduce: "Vamos a hacer que analicen las muestras externamente."
exerciseAnswer: We are going to have the samples analyzed externally.

title: Marcadores de discurso avanzados
explanation: Conectores como "That being said" o "Notwithstanding" dan un tono más formal y estructurado a tus intervenciones.
examples: That being said, we still need to confirm the timeline.
Having said that, the client seemed satisfied with the proposal.
Notwithstanding the delay, the quality remained consistent.
exercisePrompt: Traduce: "Dicho esto, seguimos necesitando confirmar el plazo."
exerciseAnswer: That being said, we still need to confirm the deadline.

title: Presente simple vs presente continuo
explanation: El presente simple es para rutinas, hechos y horarios fijos; el presente continuo es para algo que está pasando ahora mismo o es temporal.
examples: I usually check my email first thing in the morning.
We're testing a new batch right now.
She works in the lab, but this week she's covering reception.
exercisePrompt: Traduce: "Normalmente reviso los pedidos los lunes, pero esta semana los estoy revisando a diario."
exerciseAnswer: I usually check the orders on Mondays, but this week I am checking them daily.

title: Pasado simple vs pasado continuo
explanation: El pasado continuo describe una acción en curso que fue interrumpida por otra (en pasado simple) — muy útil para contar incidencias.
examples: We were testing the batch when the machine stopped.
I was writing the report when he called.
The line was running fine until the power went out.
exercisePrompt: Traduce: "Estábamos revisando el pedido cuando llegó el email del cliente."
exerciseAnswer: We were checking the order when the client's email arrived.

title: Comparativos y superlativos
explanation: Para adjetivos cortos se añade -er/-est; para los largos se usa more/most. Algunos son irregulares (good-better-best).
examples: This formula is cheaper than the last one.
It's the most expensive ingredient we use.
The new supplier is better than the old one.
exercisePrompt: Traduce: "Este proveedor es más rápido pero el otro es el más barato."
exerciseAnswer: This supplier is faster but the other one is the cheapest.

title: "going to" vs "will"
explanation: "Going to" es para planes ya decididos; "will" es para decisiones espontáneas, promesas u ofrecimientos en el momento de hablar.
examples: We're going to launch the product in March.
I'll check that for you right now.
I think it will rain later.
exercisePrompt: Traduce: "Vamos a lanzar la nueva fórmula el mes que viene." (plan ya decidido)
exerciseAnswer: We are going to launch the new formula next month.

title: Primer condicional
explanation: Para situaciones reales o probables en el futuro: if + presente simple, + will + infinitivo.
examples: If the test fails, we will repeat it.
If you send the sample today, I'll review it tomorrow.
We won't approve it if the results are not clear.
exercisePrompt: Traduce: "Si el cliente confirma hoy, enviaremos la muestra mañana."
exerciseAnswer: If the client confirms today, we will send the sample tomorrow.

title: "have to" / "must" (obligación)
explanation: "Must" expresa una obligación que sientes tú mismo o una regla fuerte; "have to" es más neutral, a menudo por una norma externa.
examples: We have to submit the report by Friday.
You must wear gloves in the lab.
I must remember to call the supplier.
exercisePrompt: Traduce: "Tenemos que enviar la muestra antes del viernes."
exerciseAnswer: We have to send the sample before Friday.

title: Present perfect con ever/never/just/already/yet
explanation: Se usa para hablar de experiencias sin decir cuándo exactamente pasaron, o de algo que acaba de pasar / todavía no ha pasado.
examples: Have you ever worked with this supplier?
We've just received the new batch.
I haven't finished the report yet.
exercisePrompt: Traduce: "Todavía no hemos recibido la confirmación del cliente."
exerciseAnswer: We haven't received the client's confirmation yet.

title: can/could/be able to
explanation: "Can" es para habilidad o permiso en presente; "could" para el pasado o para pedir algo con más cortesía; "be able to" se usa cuando necesitas otros tiempos verbales.
examples: Can you send me the file, please?
I couldn't attend the meeting yesterday.
We'll be able to confirm the price next week.
exercisePrompt: Traduce: "No pude asistir a la reunión, pero podré confirmar el precio la semana que viene."
exerciseAnswer: I couldn't attend the meeting, but I will be able to confirm the price next week.

title: Preposiciones de tiempo y lugar (in/on/at)
explanation: "At" para horas y puntos concretos, "on" para días y fechas, "in" para meses, años y periodos más largos.
examples: The meeting is at 10 o'clock, on Monday.
We launched the product in March.
The samples are in the fridge, on the second shelf.
exercisePrompt: Traduce: "La reunión es a las 3 el lunes, en la sala de reuniones."
exerciseAnswer: The meeting is at 3 on Monday, in the meeting room.

title: Question tags básicos
explanation: Son preguntas cortas al final de una frase para confirmar algo o buscar acuerdo — si la frase es afirmativa, la coletilla es negativa, y viceversa.
examples: You work in quality control, don't you?
This isn't the final version, is it?
We can send it tomorrow, can't we?
exercisePrompt: Traduce con question tag: "Trabajas con el proveedor nuevo, ¿verdad?"
exerciseAnswer: You work with the new supplier, don't you?

title: Subjuntivo formal (mandative)
explanation: Tras verbos/adjetivos que expresan necesidad o recomendación (suggest, recommend, essential, vital), el verbo va en infinitivo sin "to" y sin marcar tercera persona — un registro muy formal.
examples: It is essential that the report be submitted by Friday.
We recommend that she review the data again.
It's vital that this issue not be ignored.
exercisePrompt: Traduce en registro formal: "Es esencial que el informe se envíe antes del viernes."
exerciseAnswer: It is essential that the report be submitted before Friday.

title: Inversión tras adverbios limitantes/negativos
explanation: Al empezar la frase con adverbios como "Under no circumstances", "Rarely", o "Not until", el sujeto y el verbo auxiliar se invierten — un recurso muy formal y enfático.
examples: Under no circumstances should this formula be released without testing.
Not until the results arrived did we understand the issue.
Rarely have we seen such a fast turnaround.
exercisePrompt: Traduce con inversión: "Bajo ninguna circunstancia debería enviarse esto sin revisar."
exerciseAnswer: Under no circumstances should this be sent without reviewing.

title: Cleft sentences avanzadas
explanation: Estructuras como "It wasn't until... that" o "What... was" ponen un énfasis muy marcado sobre una parte concreta de la frase, típico de un registro cuidado.
examples: It wasn't until we changed suppliers that quality improved.
What concerns me most is the lack of documentation.
It was only after the audit that the issue came to light.
exercisePrompt: Traduce: "No fue hasta que cambiamos de proveedor que la calidad mejoró."
exerciseAnswer: It wasn't until we changed suppliers that quality improved.

title: Nominalización para registro formal
explanation: Convertir un verbo en sustantivo (decide → decision, fail → failure) da un tono más formal e impersonal, muy usado en informes y comunicación escrita.
examples: The decision to postpone the launch was unanimous.
The failure to meet the deadline caused delays.
Their reluctance to share the data was noted.
exercisePrompt: Traduce con nominalización: "El fallo en cumplir el plazo causó retrasos."
exerciseAnswer: The failure to meet the deadline caused delays.

title: Elipsis y sustitución avanzada
explanation: En un registro cuidado, se evita repetir palabras usando sustitución (so/neither + auxiliar) o elipsis (omitiendo lo ya dicho).
examples: I'd love to attend, but I can't.
She hasn't finished the report, and neither have I.
He said he'd call, and so he did.
exercisePrompt: Traduce con sustitución: "Ella no ha terminado el informe, y yo tampoco."
exerciseAnswer: She hasn't finished the report, and neither have I.

title: Matización avanzada (downtoning)
explanation: Frases como "I couldn't help but wonder" o "It would be remiss of me not to mention" suavizan una opinión fuerte sin perder claridad — muy propio de un registro casi nativo.
examples: I couldn't help but wonder whether the timeline was realistic.
It would be remiss of me not to mention the cost implications.
One might argue that the approach was overly cautious.
exercisePrompt: Traduce con matización: "No pude evitar preguntarme si el plazo era realista."
exerciseAnswer: I couldn't help but wonder whether the timeline was realistic.

title: Modales perfectos con matiz
explanation: "Should have" es un consejo tardío o crítica; "needn't have" indica que algo se hizo pero no era necesario; "ought to have" es muy similar a "should have" pero más formal.
examples: You should have told me sooner.
We needn't have rushed the report — the deadline was extended.
They ought to have consulted the client first.
exercisePrompt: Traduce: "No hacía falta que te apresuraras — el plazo se amplió." (usa needn't have)
exerciseAnswer: You needn't have rushed — the deadline was extended.

title: Frontalización para énfasis (fronting)
explanation: Adelantar un complemento u objeto al principio de la frase, en vez del orden habitual, añade un fuerte énfasis — recurso retórico de registro alto.
examples: A risk worth taking, this is not.
Highly unlikely, in my opinion, is a delay of that magnitude.
Little did we know how much the project would change.
exercisePrompt: Traduce con frontalización: "Poco sabíamos lo complicado que sería este proyecto."
exerciseAnswer: Little did we know how complicated this project would be.

title: Colocaciones idiomáticas de registro formal
explanation: Expresiones fijas como "at the eleventh hour" o "iron out the details" son naturales en un hablante casi nativo, pero suenan forzadas si se traducen literalmente del español.
examples: We managed to iron out the details before the deadline.
The contract was signed at the eleventh hour.
Let's not lose sight of the bigger picture.
exercisePrompt: Traduce usando una colocación idiomática: "Conseguimos resolver los detalles antes del plazo."
exerciseAnswer: We managed to iron out the details before the deadline.

title: Conectores de cohesión avanzados
explanation: Conectores como "Notwithstanding", "Insofar as", o "Be that as it may" dan un tono muy formal y preciso, propio de informes o correspondencia de alto nivel.
examples: Notwithstanding the delay, the results were positive.
Insofar as the data allows, we can confirm the trend.
Be that as it may, the deadline remains unchanged.
exercisePrompt: Traduce: "A pesar del retraso, los resultados fueron positivos." (usa Notwithstanding)
exerciseAnswer: Notwithstanding the delay, the results were positive.
